questions.question: Explain, using a cake, why 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 are equal.
questions.expected_answer: Cut a cake in half and take one half. Cut each half into 2 to make quarters, and the share is 2 of the 4 pieces. Cut each quarter into 2 to make eighths, and the share is 4 of the 8 pieces. The amount of cake never changed, so the three fractions are equal.

questions.question: Write 3/4 as an equivalent fraction in twelfths and explain.
questions.expected_answer: Multiply the top and bottom by 3: 3/4 is 9/12. Cutting every quarter into 3 pieces makes twelfths, and the 3 quarters become 9 twelfths.

questions.question: Use twelfths to decide which is bigger, 2/3 or 3/4.
questions.expected_answer: Multiply the top and bottom of 2/3 by 4 to get 8/12. Multiply the top and bottom of 3/4 by 3 to get 9/12. 9/12 is bigger than 8/12, so 3/4 is bigger than 2/3.
